BeamNG.drive is a realistic soft-body physics simulator developed by BeamNG. BeamNG.drive not only lets you drive realistic cars, it also lets you crash them into each other! While the racing may not appeal to those who don’t use a wheel, the game’s awesome physics can be easily enjoyed using a gamepad or even a keyboard. It’s worth mentioning I’m in the camp of mainly crashing things into each other so I won’t focus so much on anything more heavily related to racing.
While I’ve only recently received the game I have been following its progress for around a year and it has received regular updates during that time. Obviously it’s still not a finished product but what’s already in the game is good and if the devs continue working on the game it’s only going to get better.
Full Disclosure: A review copy was provided by the developer.
As you’d expect from a realistic simulator, it’s a good looking game. Of course it’s not to the point of being photo-realistic but everything looks good enough in the game to make it feel about as real as a simulator can be. The UI and menus are absolutely spot on for the game, the speedometer is usually the only visible UI element and it’s only visible when you’re using the third person camera, it’s out of the way otherwise which certainly helps your driving if you’re just smashing things into each other. The menus are simple and easy to use and even when you’re using the menu you can still see most of the screen (which is good because you’ll occasionally want to be editing your option while playing the game, for example if you want to increase gravity while you’re mid-air to utterly obliterate your car).
BeamNG.drive’s two (current) game modes are Scenarios and Free Roam with a Career mode coming soon. The Scenario game mode features pre-made scenarios from the developers themselves as well as any user made scenarios that you download from the BeamNG website. Generally these scenarios are either races or car tests but some of them are a little more exciting (not to say the others aren’t fun) such as scenarios where you drive a police car and you have to stop a speeding vehicle. The Free Roam mode is pretty much self-explanatory, you can choose one of the game’s eleven maps with any of the game’s thirteen vehicles. You can also use other in-game objects here too like a giant hamster wheel or a canon. Free Roam is where you’ll be making your own scenarios if you’re so inclined but as far as I can tell you need the Scenario editing mod from the website to do this. But if you don’t want to make your own scenarios it can be a lot of fun to just drive your car around one of the Island maps or smash it into things in the gridmap full of ramps and other fun things.
Realism is of course the most important part of a simulation game and, as far as I can tell, BeamNG.drive is pretty realistic. Now it is worth mentioning that I don’t drive and I’ve never seen a real car crash but I reckon I’ve got enough experience as a passenger and as someone who has a decent knowledge of physics to comment on this aspect of the game.
Of course it’s hard to tell when playing with a gamepad rather than a wheel but vehicle handling seems pretty solid. As far as I know there’s no traction control for the vehicles in the game so things do get a little bit skiddy from time to time but the cars all feel pretty weighty (apart from the three wheel Pigeon of course). The soft body physics are out of this world good, I don’t think I’ve come across a game with better. Obviously slamming things into each other looks good but it’s when you misjudge a corner and go head on into a tree that you really see just how powerful the engine is.
(If you like Sandbox physics games)
BeamNG.drive may be lacking in 'defined' content but it more than makes up for it with its incredibly realistic soft body physics and good graphics. If you want a realistic driving sim or you just want to crash things into each other then chances are you’ll enjoy this game!

This game has offered me hundreds of hours of entertainment, and some of the greatest gaming experiences of my life.
This is not a review of the contents of the game itself, but rather the effects of playing the game with a large community of players.
Playing online on a server with an active community forces you to get into diplomacy, which is a first in any game for me.
Other similar pvp-oriented games do of course offer diplomacy, but never have I had to ride up to the gates of a great kingdom and ask for assistance, and end up a vassal for a kingdom much larger and powerful than my own.
When starting a conflict or a war, you have to pick sides, maintain alliances, choose whether or not you're strong enough to sustain vassals, that in return will provide you with their military strength.
You have the option to display your strength to neighbouring kingdoms and risk war to prevent being attacked, or just lie down belly up and hope they take pity on you.
The allies you choose, can result in major server-wide conflicts escalating, and breaking alliances can have the same effect.
The choices of one kingdom affects all kingdoms.
These are all features created by the community itself. Not because the game rewards it, but because the game allows it. And it's something that really puts Life is Feudal apart from other similar games.
I give this game a big thumbs up, and I'm looking forward to the finished product.

This game was one of the original strategy RPGs that defined the genre. LOMSE got the formula right so many years ago, and so many strategy RPGs that have followed have failed to live up to my expectations due to the standard this game set. Despite the outdated graphics, this game is still very fun and has a great deal of depth. Play as Life, Order, Chaos, Water, Fire, Earth or Air as you attempt to defeat the evil Balkoth and ensure the continuation of your people. You are a lord of magic, leading your faith in this challenging game. Once you win one game, you can play as Balkoth and destroy the world if you want.
The game is filled with all manner of creative artifacts (weapons, armor, rings, amulets, scrolls, and potions) for your Lord and Champions to utilize. There are all manner of dungeons to explore. Battles take place on a tactical map, whereby you can utilize your horsemen, archers, mages, and ground units strategically to help win the battle. Battles are real time, but the primary map is turn based. Production of units is instantaneous if you have the resources, but resource production is turn based. The resources in this game are gold, ale, magic crystals, and fame. Gold is primarily used for ranged units, ale for melee units, and crystals for magic units, of which there are all manner of magic creatures to call to your aid depending on your faith.
Beyond the base game, there are also several scenario games you can play. For example, play as the wizard Merlin looking for hte next king of camelot.
If you are a fan of either RPGs or strategy games, I can say with confidence that you will love this game. That is, supposing you are not one of those that has to see sweet graphics in order to be interested. I can tell you that the graphics actually were pretty sweet at the time this game came out. I've kept coming back to this game since I first got it in the late 90s, but now I finaly have a version that works better with new operating systems. Maybe if we get lucky, they will come out with a sequel someday.
Impressions Games no longer exists, and Sierra, who first published this game, later was bought and became a subsidary of Vivendi, from which rebellion bought the rights to Lords of Magic prior to the Vivendi buyout by activision. So the chances are slim, but who knows, maybe rebellion will take some time away from sniper elite, or the newly made Sierra (re-established in 2014 by Activision) buys back the rights and makes one? Long time fans can only hope. And as for my hope, it is only that you enjoy this awesome game.

I am writing this review to showcase my Let’s Play of this game, which I recently released on my YouTube channel named; Mangs.
Lords of Magic was the first game I ever played as a child. Gifted to me on Christmas eve when I had just turned 9 years old, it was a game that stirred my interest for turn-based strategy.  I did not even understand the language, but I loved the graphics, sounds and especially the music. I played this game so much I ended up having to re-buy it twice due to breaking two of my CD’s.
Looking back at it 20 years later, I am amazed how far this game was ahead of its time compared to other games. While it may be clunky, slow and outdated by today’s standards, it poses a real challenge to even the most hardened veteran, and it’s systems are still complex and tricky to figure out. The game’s diplomacy system, while not terribly advanced, still allows you to be somewhat tactical by befriending other nations via the use of gifts and trades. The magic is very tricky, requiring you to research your spells before using them, but once you get going, magic becomes a terribly force on the battlefield, allowing you to wipe out entire armies with your wizard alone. This would be a problem if the game was named anything else than “Lords of Magic”, but with magic being such a central theme of the game, I am okay with it being as devastating as it is.
For all the love I have for this game, it can be terribly frustrating at times though. Even your toughest  units die so incredibly fast in battle. Saving them feels like a hopeless and sometimes monotonous task, and in order to succeed you HAVE to babysit your units like crazy until they start leveling up. Even at max level however, they usually do not last very long on the battlefield, but at least they have a fighting chance.
I also heavily dislike the auto-calculate feature that allows you to resolve battles with the click of a button, as it goes way too easy on the player, often tempting you to auto-calculate simply because the result is more desirable. I suggest not using this feature at all if you want to have a good experience with this game, unless it is to quickly get rid of a small, meaningless army that would otherwise not pose a threat to you.
20 years later, this game continues to captivate and amaze me. The music, graphics and sounds are timeless to me, and completely one-of-a-kind. If you enjoyed games like Heroes of Might and Magic as a kid, you will absolutely love Lords of Magic. I seriously recommend it!

Lords of Magic: Special Edition is a Turn Based strategy game with RPG elements (and an RPG type game mode),  developed by Impressions Games and released Nov 19, 1997
The story of Lords of magic takes place in the land of Urak the whole land has been laid to ash by the sorcerer Balkoth. The rest of the explanation is left up to interpretation... You choose your class, and faction/faith and set out to save your people... or die again and again because there's so much in this game you didn't know about before, but each time you come back a little more prepared and understanding a bit more then before.
Truth be told, I don't know that I'm really qualified to speak about Lords of Magic because I didn't play it as a kid. and even now, I'll need to spend many more hours before I'm familiar enough that I might actually stand a chance while playing.
However, I did play the heck out of Lords of the Realm 2. So how different could a game made by the same developers be? ...turns out the difference could be astronomical. To me the only similarity is the music (A+ music btw, absolutely love it) and the battles.
Lets just start with the basic set up for a Lords of Magic Game
You first chose between three classes: Warrior, Mage, and Thief. Each class has it's own strengths weaknesses and class abilities.
Then you choose your faction or "faith". There are eight faiths; Life Death, Earth, Air, Fire, Water, Order, and Chaos.
Again, each faith is specialized in a certain ways and with certain types of units.
Then you jump into the game and let the complexity begin!
It's not actually THAT bad when you're first learning how to play. As long as you just accept that things are going to end badly for you. You don't even need to battle, you can just let the computer Auto Calculate the battle for you.
You have several different resources which are used for upgrading, hiring mercenaries, recruiting new troops, and paying your troops wages. There's Fame (You can beg for gold, in exchange for fame, or horde fame and get more people who join your cause!), Followers (followers can be put to work, or used to recruit troops), Gold, Gem's (Gem's are a bit tricky, they're used for magic, be it healing your troops in the capital city, or summoning creatures and magic users, and lastly pints of ale (Just another currently, and if I learned anything in Lords of the Realm 2, it's one of the most important! who doesn't love a good 'ol drunk  jk).
Everything is turn based, so you can move a certain distance with your army, and then end turn to receive new resources. The battles are real time though. (So very similar to Lords of the Realm mechanically speaking)
I don't know if I can articulate this very well, but at times I felt more like an "Adventuring party" which is going out exploring and hero journeying.. rather then a king protecting a country. Someone who has played longer and more might be able to articulate it better, but hopefully this review helps. Lords of Magic is a solid game, and highly recommended if you're interested in strategy games.

I just beat this game today. I've been waiting for this moment since I was 11. Hot damn does it feel good.
Alright, so way back when I was a wee tadpole, my mom got me a Sierra Strategy Triple Pack for Christmas. Cyberstorm, Caesar II, and Rise of Rule of Empires was on it. It also had a demo for LoM and I wound up playing that far more than the other games. Problem was, I was 11 and couldn't just go out and buy my own games. My mom wasn't any help either. And thus, for all these years past, I was never able to sit down and give LoM a real try. So thank you Steam for giving me this.
LoM is a strategy game where the goal is to defeat Balkoth, the evil Lord of Death who is attempting at sinking the land of Urak into the dark clutches of a death god. To do this you must build your army, liberate your Great Temple from enemy clutches, and forge various alliances with the other elemental factions in the game (Air, Water, Order, Chaos, Fire, Light, Earth, and Death.) Each faction has its own strengths and weaknesses so there's a ton of replayability depending on which you choose. Do you begin with a sturdy Warrior based Earth faction, strong in melee offense or do you start with a Thief based Light faction, excelling in ranged archery?
LoM seems a little overwhelming at first but it's actually quite simple as there are only so many variables to pay attention to. Your resources are limited to Crystals, Ale, Gold, and Fame, with each Faction having their own dependencies on one more than the other. These resources are used to fuel upkeep costs of units and for creating them. Liberating various locations such as gold mines, crystal mines, and breweries provide these resources each round. It's that simple. Once you learn the pacing for each faction, playing through the game is largely up to you. LoM can be incredibly short or incredibly long, depending on how effective you are and how much RNG loves you during your attempts. This is a game that is meant to be played many, many times so never feel like you're enbroiling yourself into a 100 hour campaign every time you start.
The downsides to the game lie mostly with the RNG: some attempts the AI takes a more even pace; others its on the juice, plowing straight through you. Nothing felt better than having Balkoth roll up into my capital within the first 30 turns. I died very quickly. Sometimes enemy units move in a logical fashion; another time, Balkoth sat over the ocean, mere pixels out of my range, for nearly 20 rounds just to spite me, unmoving. If the AI is feeling cruel, you can get steamrolled very quickly in this game. Just gotta hit New Game and start again...
I cannot express how happy I am that this game has held up after all of these years. A chapter of my life has finally been completed. If you're a fan of classic strategy, you'll find an immense amount of fun with LoM.

Level your character up to level 31 to gain ability points for abilities that don't leave you a walking mewling kitten ripe for an easy PvP kill or quick Monster mob overwhelming.
When you die you lose everything. All levels, all Ability points, All items and cash on your body. You must start over at level 1. You can stash items in an account bank in the safe zone to stockpile weapons, ammo, and food for yourself. When you die you are randomly generated and put on the map. Enjoy the long trek through PvP sniper hell & Monsters to get back to a safe zone to get items from your account stash. Don't take too much though, you will soon get a PvP bullet to the head or a random swarm of monsters that quickly overwhelm the amount of ammo you have on your person.

This review is coming through a heavily nostalgic tint, but Lords of Magic is probably THE defining game of its genre. . . whatever genre that is.  A bit like Masters of Magic, this is a dudes-on-a-map strategy game, where you balance realtime combat with resource management. You play one of seven faiths fighting against the forces of Death.  You recruit heroes (Warriors, Mages, and Thieves) which lead armies of fighters, archers, and magical creatures.  I had this game on CD-ROM so my steam hours don't reflect it, but you will get tons of hours out of this game.  One of the best parts:  once you master one particular faith (Air, Fire, Water, Earth, Life, Death, Order, or Chaos), playing another one is a whole different experience.  Once you beat the game once, it unlocks Death as a playable faith, which is a great challenge in itself. The Special Edition shipped with pre-rendered quest games (one hidden), which are a delight to play.  You also get more maps to play once you master the main one, and a map editor that allows you to create your own.
It's not without its flaws though.  The graphics did not age well, though the characters do have their charm.  The combat is wonky, and you have to really learn the system. . . at the beginning it will be overwhelming.  The AI isn't that bright, and I am not sure if the steam version ships with a very game breaking difficulty bug. . . but it hasn't showed up for me yet.  There are some ways you can really game the system too. If you're having alot of trouble pick Order, Water, or Life, and tinker with the hero editor.  If all else fails, play a Water mage with the Staff of Drowning, which is essentially a hidden 'very easy' mode.
If you like strategy games or fantasy games, give this piece of gaming history a try.

Sniper Elite V2 puts you into the WWII setting in Berlin, 1941. You obviously should play the first game before this, but some of you didn't, which I'm guilty of too. I feel that after playing the first 3 missions of the game, the review was ready to be spit out. I personally like this game, and the reasons so I will say. Now the gameplay is very nice, giving you a challenge the whole way through the mission, which I like. Unlike COD, this game takes the use of your brain and putting it to work. You can't run in throught the mission and shoot, hell no, not in this game. You can easily die running into the mission, which I'm guilty of the first couple times. You can easily be picked off by one or two enemys by running in, but in COD you can take on 10-15, which is insanely absurd. Which is mainly why I don't like COD too much, but the zombies mode and campaign are alright. So, in order to not get killed so much is to have the enemy come to you, you don't come to them because 2-3 shots can kill you right off the bat.
Now to talk about the graphics and the enviroment. The enviroment is great, it gives that vibe to the whole WWII scene, having to do with flying planes, destroyed buildings, tanks, roadblocks, exploded vehicles, you name it, the game has it. The graphics are beautiful, running Sniper Elite on a 1080p resolution and the ultra settings preset made this game look beautiful, which contributed to the game being so good to me personally. But, the water and smoke looks like poop! The water looks like a plastic sheet put over the ground, not to mention that stepping in it had no splashing effect which made the water so lifeless like it wasn't even water. The game developers need to put some physics into the water and smoke, or it'll just make the enviroment seem more lifeless and bland. The smoke from a far distance looks good, but up close it looks like it was made with the Microsoft default Paint program you have in the Start menu. The smoke also has no density to it, making it bland just like the water. Again, the developers should've spent more time on the smoke and water effects. Anyways, I forgive it since the rest of the enviroment looks next-gen with great PC optimization giving a full 60FPS on ultra with this last-gen GeForce GTX 550 Ti Gigabyte OC that I carry in this PC.
Now the background story, which this game doesn't really have any. The backstory to this game makes me say "What"? Now, what I mean is that there's no backstory to this game, as in the cutscenes before each mission for example Grand Theft Auto, Half-Life, and Mafia II have a backstory, which gives it's background that promotes the fuller understanding of the game, although there's a brief saying of the mission you are about to enter in this game. But, still there really isn't a backstory to the game. Now, if you don't understand what a game's "backstory" is, I'd go look up backstory on Google or whatever search engine you use. Anyways, Sniper Elite is still good even though it has its flaws to the game. Every game has its flaws. Like Grand Theft Auto IV, which has sort of a horrible PC optimization to the game.
The heartbeat system consists of mainly two things, your lung capacity to use focus time, and your health. When your heartrate goes above 80BPM you can't go into focus time, there's two reasons as to why it is over 80BPM. One: You've been shot, which brings up the heartrate, but not necessarily all the time though, there's a few times when I been hit 3 times and it still was at 70BPM. Two: You've have been either jogging or running around, which would always raise your heartrate. So, that's the heartrate system in a nutshell.
HUD elements like your objective and your weapon and ammo will disappear after an amount of about 5 seconds, which can be helpful if you need to see at the corners of your screen. That's a plus in any game.
Overall, the game's nice, the music is good. The gunshots are satisfying when you snipe someone overhead. The overall rating of this game is a good 8.7/10.

Horror games are a special genre. What scares one person to hell, could make somebody else just raise an eyebrow, or even come across as comical to yet another gamer. Opinions on what makes a good horror game do vary accordingly, but amidst all these discussions, there's one game that stands out:
. Almost everybody who has played this game, concedes that it is exceptionally scary, and thus succeeds wonderfully as a horror game.
The first of the two
games, it was released just five years ago, in september 2010. It's not the first horror game by its developer, Frictional Games, who earlier made the
games, but it's certainly the title that made Frictional Games famous. With the hype around the upcoming release of
, yet another Frictional title, playing through their best known horror game yet only seemed appropriate, and long overdue.
Actually I started this game already three times earlier this year, every time not finding the courage to move on after the first hour or so, out of pure fear. I only play this kind of games when it's dark outside, using headphones, in order to let them develop their full scaring potential, but with
this kind of approach just looked impossible. The past couple of weeks I finally found the courage to persevere (in complete darkness), but I was only able to play the game in small pieces, only half an hour or so on end, after which I literally had to recover.
This may seem like exaggerated, but it's not. This game is by far the scariest I've ever played. Playing as Daniel, you have to re-discover who you are and what you're doing in a medieval castle somewhere deep in the German woods. As the game progresses, the story poses more and more questions, and only at the very end did all the pieces come together for me. But it's not the story itself that's particularly scary. It's the way the game puts the player in an extremely vulnerable position, without any means of defense (no swords or guns in this one!) and only some tinderboxes and a lantern as a means to progress through the increasingly unsettling surroundings.
The game is by far the darkest I've ever played. Darkness is actually transformed into one of the game's defining elements: when standing in darkness, Daniel slowly but surely turns mad, and the only way to counter this is either to light some candles with the tinderboxes, or to light your lantern. Since lantern oil is quite scarce, I found myself constantly trying to save it as much as possible. There is a constant looming danger in the form of monsters, who are seldomly to been seen but impose terror upon the player by sound or just by thought. For when a monster finds you, it's almost surely instant death. The game manages to strike the perfect balance between slowly progressing episodes where I was fumbling around in the dark, hiding for monsters and looking for clues or letters, and some scenes where the only option was: run!
It's hard to describe in words exactly why this game got so deep under my skin, though, because it terrified me on an even deeper level that has nothing to do with graphics or game mechanics. I think the theme of man turning into a monster even worse than any monster imagineable struck a resonating chord inside me. I found myself screaming out loud at times, mostly out of utter disgust at what was happening. The game had a very unsettling effect on my, and probably that's why it took me several tries to play and finish it. It's a masterpiece in its genre, yet to be trumped.

One year anniversary email Oct 2012 "After a disastrous beta and early release and severing ties with ex publisher 505 Games, our studio have finally gotten a chance to make Dawn of Fantasy the game we always wanted."
(edited for relevance/space) Apr 2013 email "We have an ambitious plan to get rid of the last remaining issues by May 1st and so that we can switch to adding awesome new features.
Here's a brief overview of the top problems we solved in the past couple of weeks
Server stability resolved - no more server downtime
Fixed lost progress, lost unit and army rollback issues
PvP, Siege and Coop does not Out of Sync or Disconnect
Fixed the quest, Co-Op and PvP victory problems
Started the UI redesign and replaced some fonts
If you left the game because you had any of the problems above, now is the time to come back and give Dawn of Fantasy: Kingdom Wars another go."
Looking at what is there right now it feels extremely buggy, poorly designed, implemented and unfinished.
Losing units (mods will reimburse, with logs), crashing during battles (lose incurred on profile), lag during coop battles (rubberbanding), Syncing issues during pvp. Unit stances and behaviours not sticking, Unit commands not being followed. Very annoying voice spam messages and popups (deleting a voice file solved one, the mods responded they would look into the other) Resource system not working. I could go on and on.
Its a real shame as the Homeland building aspects I really enjoy, enticing me to log back in and check on the little fellas regularly. The rest is, quite frankly, and I hate to say it, crap.
The ui is poorly designed. It feels like it is trying to fight me on what I am trying to do at times. Not showing all my units when I select all peasants (I believe there is a cap of 18 units selected which does not help you find that one unit you want to garrison) Hiding units in single man stacks behind a wall with no way to find them in a timely manner as the onscreen indicators are poor, Elements of the ui requesting you to look at them (quest book and invite friend button thing) flashing repeatedly until I click recognition and then flashing again a few minutes later repeatedly. I read my goddam quests the first time! Gaahhhhhh! Its like a facebook game!
You have a world map where the "mmo" takes place. This consists of a static map which is nice enough. You will never see another player on this map. This map is for you, To meet (fight) other players you move around declaring your looking for pvp and hoping that the area you are in has someone there. The system will tell you when a match is found. So its more like a lobby in the multiplayer sense. With an unnecessary visual element. The map for single player contains npc towns which you can visit(very rudimentary diplomacy), siege(coop or single) and visit for quests/selling/buying/trainging. It all just feels tacked on and has done since the beginning.
I feel like I have been harsh in writing this but I feel it has had more than enough time to be in a decent playable state. Right now I feel nervous carrying out actions. I feel increasingly nervous the longer sieges go on in case of crash/loss. I fear sieges, not because of players but because of desyncing. I feel nervous upon logging in to find any units missing.
The positives of the game are grossly overshadowed by the problems. Of note is the nice way of earning the currency (crowns) ingame. The initial period, base building in your home instance. The fact they kept my account and it was available to me from steam after a long absence. Friendly dev interaction,
Despite all that I will probably still log in to check on my little homeland every now and then. Quickly mind you, before the immunity timer wears out.
I will continually update the review as changes occur. I will happily change the recommendation if its deserving. In march apparently big changes are happening. We shall see. Unfortunately I have heard that many times before.

THEN Reverie discontinued their own client, and even on this I7 rig I have, this game lags and stutters while games like Supreme Commander and Supreme Commander 2 - develpped around the same time and with MUCH larger worlds and literally thousands of units runs beautifully. The single player risk like portion of the game has been removed. This is strictly a PvP type game. If that's your thing, then you will like this game. I prefer single player and coop PvE.

The problem however - and you'll note other users have expressed the same concern in the Hub for this game - is that Reverie keeps releasing mega-patches but fails to address core game issues.
When, as a company, ypou get rid of something that improves performance while simiultaneously releasing more and "bigger" stuff is really taking one step forward and two steps back. If you'll pardon the trope, this COULD have been the RTS fantasy strategy game to rule them all. It isn't unfortunately so it's back to playing Medieval Total War from the physical discs for me. I am sorry Reverie, you tried but you lack focus.

I don't know what creature possessed me to buy this game. I just thought to myself, "I'll just buy this, probably laugh at it, then write a review or something".
This game makes no sense to me. It's a world full of vaguely Jar-Jar Binks-looking characters that live in some medieval fantasy world but talk in a... certain way? Let me try to explain: here's a simple sentence. "I'm going to take this over to there." The SnarfQuest translation: "I'm gonna take dis over dere." This is the exact same way I heard people talk on ROBLOX in 2010.
If the dialogue wasn't too awkward, the voice acting is even worse. And then the puns... GOD, the puns... 3 minutes into the game you can talk to the character's father who is just full of endless fish puns. They don't really need to be there and nothing would be subtracted from the game if they were removed. I don't know if they were supposed to be funny or if they were intended to make us want to do a hard-shutdown on our PCs after seeing them (which is what I did the first time).
I guess I could have withstood the bad dialogue, bad graphics, and bad voice acting if the game didn't run at 5 FPS. The only way I could get to a marginally playable 12 FPS was by putting the graphics on the lowest settings and making the game run in a 800x600 window. But this is a point-and-click adventure game, and dat's about da worst way to play dis kinda game.

Oddly enough, this mod lasts longer than all three of the Penumbra games put together at about 6~8 hours of gametime depending on how. First, I'd only recommend this mod if you have played the previous three Penumbra games. Otherwise, you will be left in the dark both for story and gameplay.
PROS:
+It's pretty much the sequel to Penumbra we've always wanted. It's more of the same terror beneath the earth.
+Amosphere is perfect. Everything about being trapped underground in a forgotten place works fine.
+Sound design is, like the other Penumbras, perfect.
+Only one or two jump scares. The rest of REAL horror, like tension building and true terror. All you need to do is catch a glimpse of somnething and go &quot♥♥♥♥♥♥ I don't wanna go down that hallway... But it's the only way out." It's great to see that the makers of this mod knew people would rather dread to think something is in the dark rather than it jumping out and shouting: "SUPPORT MY PATREON!"
+All the voice actors are good. It sounds like the original voice actors.
+I said above the mod was 6~8 hours. That's wonderful for a free mod.
MIXED:
+/-The story is all over the place. The other Penumbras had progression, and this one sorta does. It's obvious the designers were trying to extend the game's length. At one point in the story, it feels like something good will happen, a victory! ... then♥♥♥♥♥♥happens and "oh no, another unknown location of the damn facility." Oddly enough, it WORKS, but at the same time, you wonder how the story will wrap up. See below.
+/-Some of the puzzles can be confusing at times.
+/- Clarence returns. Why is this a half and half? Well, I remember him dying in Penumbra: Black Plague. Yeah, this is probably the biggest plot hole. But he's a fun dude. Very fun. Speaking of plot holes, there's one more, see below.
CONS:
-There are two points of the game where a chase happens that WILL kill you if you aren't fast enough. The first time there's a switch next to the door on the right. The second time is a light switch (pull it down) on the wall just left of the lift. I just saved you 30~45minutes of trial and error because of bad design. A small or larger light source above the switches could fix both of these issues.
-Okay, this next tid bit is sort of a spoiler but it isn't. You end up exploring old areas of the facility. So, naturally, you go back to locations to double check. You do it for both Amabel's body (since she talks to you within the first 5 minutes) then your father's corpse (because why the hell not?) It turns out: Howard, your father, is missing. There's a note next to it that says "Find him -O." What? What is this? It's never explained, or if it is, it wasn't clear enough.
-I got to the end expecting there'd be some closure, especially since Howard's body was missing, but then the "choice" came up. The problem is that the choice is ambiguous as hell. It's like somebody switched the answers on an exam that you knew 100% with an entirely different language you knew nothing about. And with that said...
-You have a 50% chance you'll choose the ending that confuses you, and just quickload to see the other. If you had chosen the one that made sense, you'll just quickload and BE confused.
CLOSING:
This 100% free mod is a worthy treat. Depsite the minor problems with the mod, the focus on more terror than jump scares (I'm eyeing you fnaf), Penumbra: Necrologue should be considered the fourth and final chapter of the Penumbra series.

The Game is great! I have over 400 hours for a reason and likely to put on a lot more.
Things to remember: its early access and not the finished game, you play on player owned servers currently and all have their own sets of guidlines and rules, also different rates and maximum skill leveling abilities. The game is very craft centric so expect some aspects to be a long grind.
So far the game is very craft centric. You can blacksmith, build homes and castles, farm, tame animals, mine and log, if you can think up a craft in a fuedal era more then likely you can do it in game. To do this you need to collect resources or work out a deal to have others collect them for you. All of this and every aspect takes time. You will spend a lot of time building up to the point you envision your character to be. This is very grindy and definetely not for everyone. If the thought of spending a day or so moving dirt to level off an area to build your cabin makes you ill then you should move along. I never thought I would enjoy it as much as I do. I some how find the game very relaxing.
I am not sure how I feel about combat. I havent done much PvP and have not leveled up those skills significantly. It however feels a little floaty to me at the moment. It however has a more urgent feel to it then other games, as death or unconsiousness bring permanent penalties, whether its just loss of property or loss of skill and attributes, you wont want to make defeat a hobby. I know seige warfare is coming if not already out and that sounds very fun.
Claiming property is relatively new. It protects your land from intruders by making it so that tresspasers can be punished without any of the negative affects associated with murdering neighbours occur to the land owner. Also gives some penalties to the tresspasser. Its a nice touch.
The graphics are beautiful, yet not otimized. I expect further improvement with that as it gets closer to a release. Some animations and sounds still require work, however the game still does an excellent job at being immersive and mostly natural.
All in All this games is very good and definetly deserves a positive rating.

First of all, your search for the ultimate car game/simulator ends RIGHT HERE and RIGHT NOW.
I'm serious. No other simulator in history has ever been as realistic as BeamNG.drive. In fact, once this sim gets popular, it could even be used in driving schools! The cars handle, perform, and DEform EXACTLY like their real life counterparts. Behind each car is a revolutionary system of nodes and beams that calculates the deformation of the car's body at 2000 times a second! Not only that, but the windows crack and shatter, and pretty much every part from the headlights to the tailpipes to the fenders to the engine can break off like they would in real life.
This is a long, in-depth review, to give you the best idea of what this is.
This is an awesome simulator! You can do anything you want with cars, trucks, boats, planes, and drive/fly them as well as smash them, crash them, and drop boulders on them (Yes, I'm not kidding). There are also numerous props you can play with such as a car shredder (two rollers close together that you can drive through) and many others in the official game. There is even a fidget spinner mod that you can DESTROY cars with. And, if you want you can put that 3 foot tall spoiler on your old Honda! The base game comes with 13 maps (aka terrains) to explore, and they range from 1 square kilometer to 4 square kilometers (there is a 16 square kilometer map coming). The developers do, however make them seem much bigger despite their real size. There is also an infinite grid map which is completely flat and empty and the ground is nothing more than a grid. In addition, there are maps created by the community that can be as big as ~350 square kilometers. Once BeamNG's engine gets optimized to the point we can have open world maps, we will start seeing even larger maps.
Here are the vehicles included with BeamNG.
Also in the base game are 20 fictional vehicles (as of last review update) based off of real-life vehicles, which are FULLY customizable in almost every aspect. In addition to in-depth customization, you also get about 10 preset configurations (trims) for every car. You can choose the one you like the most and then add/remove/change the parts on that trim to make it JUST the way you want. Here is the vehicle list:
Anyway, enough about the content. Let's get into the gameplay and physics.
Although for now there is no Career mode, this simulator is still very fun to play. There are scenarios, and they are usually coordinated time trials on a specific course on a specific terrain. Sometimes it is just for fun, like jumping a van off a ramp and landing unscathed.
And the physics, they will not get any better than this. BeamNG is the most realistic and detailed vehicle simulator to date. It simulates the behavior of vehicles from the glass breaking to the hubcaps falling off to the engine block melting. BeamNG uses a unique system for ultra-realistic vehicle behavior that yields a unique gaming experience each time. It uses beams (BEAMng) and nodes to simulate each and every part independently. The nodes connect all of the thousands of beams together, and the beams can deform, bend, and break. There are no predefined damage models. The node and beam system calculates the damage on any one section of the car. For example, if you slide past a wall in a Need For Speed game, with the front facing it slightly more than the back, the windows will probably shatter and then there will be paint scratches on random places of the car. Let's slide past that same wall in BeamNG. The mirror fell off and there is a dent in the front bumper EXACTLY where the car contacted the wall. Also a hubcap most likely fell off if the car had plastic rims.
If all that isn't enough, there is a big community on the BeamNG forums cranking out mods frequently. There are well over 200 vehicles/vehicle mods to download and well over 200 extra maps to download from the mod repository alone.
And, finally, let's talk customization. Let's take the D-15 for example. For this single vehicle, you can customize the paint job (color/decals), the tow hitch, the type of engine (I6 or 2 tiers of V8s), supercharger, lights, color, bumper type and color, suspension, body, and even the light bar to name a few. So the bottom line is, this game offers more customization options than any other driving game currently on the market. Even NFS Underground 2.
Also, in the 0.10 update, each kind of engine (inline 4, v6, etc) has its own sound!
I hope this review was helpful to any new BeamNG players. Enjoy this wonderful game!

Straight to it, Lords of Magic is one of the best. I cannot do it justice, it's really a diamond.
I've played it since the demo came out 19 years ago, and I played it yesterday.
Overall: 9/10
Game Length: Hours
Complexity: Moderate
Replay: Infinite
The music has that rare perfection, it is atmospheric, beautiful, and yet blends into the background and doesn't annoy on repeat (unlike say, Civilization I and II). The gameplay itself is fun, sensible, and keeps getting deeper the more one plays. While the rules are simple, they mingle to form complex situations. The AI is unexpected, good even by today's standards. There's tons of customization without it being overwhelming or senseless. It's endlessly replayable, every New Game plays out differently. Of course, you can always play as the main villain instead for a completely different experience, or one of the expansion Quests. There's even a complete map creator if you want more. You literally cannot run out of game to play.
Everything matters, from terrain, to spells, to flanking, to army movement, and so on, there is no aspect of the game that is 'useless' or ignorable. Now it is also likewise quite unforgiving, rarely is there a chance to take back a bad decision, it's not that any mistake will spell your doom, it's that one could. Getting yourself stuck in the zipper of imperial overreach is very much a possibility. This is a challenging game, and it does not have much tolerance for tactless blind charges, dumb is dead. It is however true, just as in real war, that sometimes a misstep could not be foreseen, or luck sides against you, and in a close battle that can be the difference that causes utter defeat. The game is only <mostly> fair, not completely fair. Even a solid victory can be Pyrrhic.
I've seen it said that the game is well balanced, or not at all. I disagree, I think it has that always-sought after and rare perfect imbalance. Yes, some Faiths are easier or harder for beginners, because their strengths are intuitive or obvious to implement. But each one can win consistently, they just use unconventional tactics, and come into their pinnacle at different stages. Like, Life infantry may be weak, but that's because they're not meant to fight, they're meant to Parry in full defense, holding the line while your archers eat up the enemy. The Air infantry make terrible infantry, because you should use them like cavalry instead. The best Fire spell harms all units on the battlefield, but Fire Mages and Elementals are resistant, making them the ideal sacrificial mercenary strike team to soften a powerful enemy army at low cost. Chaos Stickthrowers are generally mistaken to be the worst ranged units, but their attack speed is the quickest, so they lock down powerful enemy melee units if targeting it together as a group. There's always a useful method to be found. Not every Faith fights best in a traditional style, and often their true strengths are meta - such as economics, mobility, recovery, or synergy. However, the balance between preparation and tactics, skill and luck, quality vs quantity, those factors are superbly arranged.
Lords of Magic did have troubled development, it was a buggy mess that was beloved despite that, and the game wasn't completely fixed until support was discontinued. Steam offers the 3.01 version, however it retains one significant Unit ID bug that replaces Brownies (tiny weak scouts) in some low level battles with Pegasus Riders (absurdly strong late game tank). To that end I completely recommend the unofficial 3.02 patch, dedicated fans took development to the finish line, removing the last bugs and improving the menu and game interface. As always, use at your own discretion.
That said, the game shines, not for it's functional but dated graphics, but the fluff. Each and every of the 160+ spells has it's own story text, revealing the culture, legends, and life of the people of each Faith. Every dungeon has a serviceable description, that unveils a deeper moral ambiguity than you'd expect. Sure, some Paladin Lord of Order is expected to liberate a sacred statue from miscreants, but what of robbing and pillaging the estate of a wealthy ex-thief? It makes no difference mechanically, but it highlights that victory is at all costs. It clearly takes influence from the Lord of the Rings, but it absolutely makes up itself. Even the building quotes hint at a rich and full culture and history for each Faith. When it's cheesy it's homage to Conan the Barbarian, Tolkien, Beowulf, King Arthur, and other classics. Even the hefty manual is more narrative than tutorial. In short, more than anything, it's voluntarily immersive. It lets you care. It brings you in and makes it believable that there's a whole world.
The story, the music, the atmosphere, the strategy, all are crafted together masterfully to create a cohesive and fulfilling fantasy 5x - explore, expand, exploit, exterminate, and experience.

I found this game charming. Artwork graphics look nice, the audio is appropriate for its genre, and the movement system has a nice feel (aside from the jump being a bit tight). Worth the price, but definitely foreseeing some polishing in certain aspects of the game. Very bareboned arena shooter at the moment. It'll need some work for newer versions of the game.
What I liked:
- Scratches arena itch on its most basic level.
- Pretty immersive atmosphere.
- Fast paced running and gunning. (AR is loads of fun)
- Decent variety of enemies and levels for a barebone early access.
What I disliked:
- Feels rather overwhelming and no sense of "overcoming" enemies.
- It's difficult to strategize; as the monster spawning feels a bit too random.
- Explosions throw you too far.
Other things to point out:
- The game is difficult (likely intentionally), as soon as you dive in, it's a constant battle of slowly approaching enemies until you die. I personally like the difficulty, but the randomness is a little too rough.. Every game should have a moment where you've felt like you've triumpth a certain degree here and there.
- Hoping to see a configuration menu soon! Would love to tweak audio levels and motion blur effect to my liking.
- There's an exploit where monsters have an extremely difficult time reaching you on the weapon platform on the last level. Also, achievements are very wonky.
But hey! This is about the same price as a cup of coffee, and if you wanna kill 1, 2, or more hours; this is a great way to do it. It's a charming game for its price, and actually pretty fun if you take it for what it is.

Sniper Elite V2 is a bad case of a game trying to do what it isn't supposed to do.
It markets itself as a sniper game. And I will admit it is very good at that. The sniping in the game is very satisfying and interesting. It's very fun trying to line up a good shot after factoring in the bullet drop and other factors. The slow motion and X-ray effects are great, they make you feel like you're powerful.
Unfortunately, the game tries way too hard to be an action game at the same time. You spend more time sneaking around and shooting than sniping. Stealth plays an important part in the game, but it's done very poorly. There are no ways to easily kill guards silently, and your 'silent' crouch is extraordinarily slow. Simply put, stealth feels very sluggish and forced into the game. I found it a lot more satisfying just to pull out a gun and force my way through the stealth sections.
Speaking of which, the gunplay in this game is awful. The camera controls don't work very well, and the guns feel completely useless. You feel like you're using a peashooter as the enemies shrug off bullets. No to mention there are way too many of these sections in the game. Why is it called "Sniper Elite" when you're using an SMG or pistol for 50% of the game?
Overall the game is so terribly mediocre in all aspects I find it impossible to recommend. If you're looking for a really good stealth and sniping game, try the first game. But if you're looking for a competent game that doesn't bore the hell out of you, don't try this.

Despite the fact that this is a "mod", I prefer it over the original Penumbra games.
The developers did a excellent job with making it feel exactly like an official Penumbra game. They ported the models, textures, and sounds straight from the original games. Oh, they didn't just port them, they tweaked them. Textures have been reskined to look more high quality and modern. Not to mention the game mechanics play and feel very similar to the original games, only a lot less clunky. If you showed this to me without me knowing what it was, and you told me it was an official Penumbra game made by Frictional Games, I wouldn't question you.
They didn't only port things from the originals. They added their own new, custom stuff. One of them being an OST. And the OST sounds awesome. Some of the songs are spin-offs/remixes of music heard in the prior games, and others are completely new. Once again, they did a great job with making it sound like something you'd hear in an official Penumbra game.
One surprising thing is how long this is. Its longer than any of the original games. I think it took me about 10 hours to beat. And it doesn't even get tedious. You visit lots of different location themes. The original games had a specific theme for each game. In Overture you were in the old mines. In Black Plague you were in the modern facility. In Requiem you were in some weird alien/dream world. But in Necrologue, you visit them all in one game! It may sound like a cluster, but they all went together really well, and the transitions didn't feel out of place. You even revisit some areas that were in the originals.
Something that I really liked were the enemies. Unlike the original games, which only had a few enemy types, or even none, this has 6 different ones. They brought back ALL the enemies from previous games, so expect some giant spiders, or even a feral dog or two. Don't worry, though. They added some NEW enemy types, too! Well, technically they aren't "new," they're actually unused ones from when the original games were in development. It's awesome, because it's rare for an Amnesia mod to have custom enemies. Let alone 6 different ones.
I have mixed feelings about the voice acting. Most of the voices in of themselves didn't sound bad, the worst part was when they tried to substitute the voices of the original characters. For example, Clarence hardly sounds like Clarence at all. Everybody else sounded good/decent though. (I'm talking about the English version. I don't know how good the voice actors for the other languages are.)
Unfortunately, since this is a foreign mod, there is some broken English. Mainly the notes and some loading screens had a few grammatical errors in them. Nothing too bad.
By far the worst part about this mod is how unstable it is. They obviously didn't test this on lower graphics settings. If your Texture Quality isn't set to High, the mod is unplayable. Even if your computer is capable of playing on maxed out settings, you will still experience a few fatal crashes. Those aren't persistent, though.
Despite the above issues, this mod is arguably better than the original Penumbra games. This is the final installment Frictional Games should've made.

Before we begin: I bought the basic game version in which you have to unlock everything, and my review is based on that. At time of this posintg I have 90% of cards unlocked, and I've played plenty of multiplayer.
Short answer: 7/10. The core of the game delivers as promised, but certain aspects of the UI need polish, and certain design desicions will upset people.
Pros
-Full deck customisation: You can choose exactly what cards from your collection you want in the deck, with full 5 color support if you so choose. You can add lands in any combintion. The editor even lets you do stupid things like add Islands to an all red deck. The editor stat breakdown make things like your mana curve and color wighting clear.
-AI knows what it is doing: the AI is fantastic, easily on par with DotP 2014 but entirely capable of dealing with the literally infinite combination of deck designs
-Match UI performance improvement: The playfield UI responds much better. There is no real framerate lag to be had, unlike previous games.
-Card collecting mechanic: You are rewarded bosters for single player or multiplayer matches. Cards are obtained in random boosters, however the game ensures it does not give you card you cannot use (like a 5th copy of the same common). This makes the grinding relatively painless as you dont end up with hundreds of dead cards. As a result the grind is the least severe of all DotP games.
Cons:
-Out of game UI is horrible: There is no persistent multiplayer lobby. You cannot change decks while in a multiplayer lobby. Menu transitions are incredibly slow for no apparent reason due to a weird 'fade to white' transition effect. All of these are direct steps backward from 2014 and are very unlikely to get fixed. All in all this adds a lot of annoyance to playing.
- No cards for losing multi: This is mostly a quality of life thing, but you cannot earn cards for say losing x matches in multi, or even coming second in a 4 player game. This forces you to grind away in single player just to be competative. It makes getting new people involved in the game difficult
-Certain game modes missing: This is not so much an issue for me as others, but sealed deck and Two-Headed Giant modes are both gone, and man is the internet butthurt about it. A lot of the negative opinion of the game is being generated by this point alone.
-Some cards only obtainable through real cash transaction, or not obtainable at all: AI have cards in their decks you cannot collect, and odd choice considering it would literally be flicking a switch to make them obtaininable in a booster (they would have to be fully coded for the AI to use them). Some cards only accesible by RMT, and then its randomised booster. Since you cannot collect junk copies of cards you'd need to spend about 30 bucks on premium boosters to get everything. A lot of negative community opinion is that this is P2W, but frankly its not a big deal, the cards arent essential.
All in all, the game is fantastic, but definitely read up on the difference in features before making a purchase. If you don't care about two headed giant and like the single player AI, then you will definitely like this game.

Being a big fan of the previous MTG online games, I preordered this game, god do I regret it now, I thought the 10 dollar price was really nice for what I was getting. Where do I even start, they removed the most played format, where previous MTG online games had things such as Archenemy, or planechase, you get my gist, there is none. No extra format and they even removed one. They've said its because it did not look well with the current design of the board, and that certain card interactions was too good. I can understand the second point, whereas the first being a terrible excuse.
Even then, you do not remove such a feature for that reason, if you don't like the OP card interactions that can be made, its still better than removing such a beloved feature, far better.
The menu is absolutely abysmal, there is white everywhere, at all parts of the game, even after transition froma dark cinematic, which hurt my eyes. It is terribly wonky and slow to navigate with tablets being in mind and not the most used way to play it, computer. The fact that they try to make it work well on tablet is great, but again, really not the way to go. They could at least have made a few adjustments to the PC title.
There is still so much bad I could say about this game, but I am going to stop beating around the bush and get to the worst feature of the game, saving the best for last.
The microtransaction system. Previous titles let you pay a minor amount of money to unlock the entire deck instantly instead of unlocking cards for winning with the deck. As well as paying to get those cards in foil. They'd put a slightly higher charge, but nothing extreme on new decks added after the release of the game, long enough to justify releasing additional decks, as well as expansions. Sounds great to me. Previous titles had codes that'd be released now and then to unlock cards for all the decks. Accessible for everyone as far as I know.
This time around, they have put a incredibly high charge on unlocking all the cards you can unlock from playing the campaign, not too bad, no need to buy that really. But they have added promo packs, 15 packs at about 2€ or whatever currency you use. Bumping the DAY ONE price for full content in the game up to 40€. As well as breaking multiplayer mode for people who are not willing to invest more money into the game.
Even if you are a long time fan of the online Magic series, do not get this game.

I was bought this game as a gift from a friend after watching the trailer, adding it to my wishlist, and then all but forgetting about it. I will start by saying the more I play the more enjoyable it has gotten. When I first tried it I was confused, the UI was hard to read and understand, but lo and behold you can customize the UI. you can customize most things in the game actually, you want a plasma gun with a flamethrower underslung? sure. How bout a minigun with a rocketlauncher and corrosive rounds? no problem. tired of shooting your enemies? setup turrets and casually repair them as the battle rages. I heard you like grenades, how bout dat double grenade incendiary frag, flashbang EMP, corrosive smoke, mix and match who cares. wanna be fast, use the light armor, wanna be faster? install double speed servos and jump over vehicles, tired of getting murdered? go heavy with a bunch of extra armor and shrug off some small arms fire. Or go medium and enjoy a bit of both. no level requirments to equip, jsut a kind of resource pool to draw from as you play more. I did not feel under equipped when i started but increasing your limits is quit fun. got a friend? surf his gunship in land battles and show everyone your gnar flying repairman skills. use caution while pressing shift in the buggy, you'll break your neck with that kind of acceleration. hover tanks you say? why yes they got em. fighters, interceptors, assault fighters, dropships, bombers, corvettes, destroyers, frigates, battle ships, stations, boarding of enemy vessels, and firing missiles at your self to kill thier dropships.  you can customize all the smaller ships, all the land vehicles, the gunship, the mechs, the match options are fairly comprehensive. some maps have two game modes but with changes to the scene like night battle for one day for the other ect... with about 20 choices including "duplicate" maps, but they feel quite different between incursion, and territories game modes. oh you can strap a shield to your rifle and take your cover with you, and you can use space flashbangs with the mines on space craft. decent AI, but you can issue orders (either as commander issuing orders to squad leaders then the differ to thier men, or as a squad leader controlling only a  handfull of units) either in first person by pressing C, then numbers to go through your selections, taget an enemy and tap C,1,1 and all your guys try to murder them. or you can issue orders by the map which is a 3d hologram lookin deal that changes color with your hud settings. The only things this game needs in my opinion are: a jetpack, more optimizations or w/e grants more fps (sometimes the graphical setting dont change my fps, between ultra, and dog doo presets) but it usually holds a steady framrate of 30 for me (980ti, amd fx8350,16gb ram) MORE PLAYERS!!!! but the bots are fun, I have a buddy i play with and we have had as many as 6 stragglers join us but I would love to see a full game of humans. at the pricepoint of 18 bucks it is worth every penny. I would also like to see customization further implemented with the capital ships, corvettes, frigates, and destroyers. I really have no negative views for the game only a thirst for more, but we all know how that goes.

I'm hoping however that Wizards of the Coast will come out with a massive update to 'fix' the issues many peple have with the changes they made from previous DOTP's.
PROS: -Unlocks through 'free' boosters packs after you win a duel.
(DO NOT purchase the complete edition as that only unlocks these cards and takes out       the whole point of the game)
-Deck building. A welecome change even though it has its challenges. See cons.
-addictive fun once you have a deck that you like to play multiplayer.
CONS:
-starter decks. vague discription and then you are stuck with it. no preview, nothing. Will take time to build a capable deck meaning it will be a frustrating start.
- terrible UI, hard to do what you want it to do
- removal of co-op (2-headed giants), challenges, archenemy.
-NO ability to 'rematch' in online play.
- Custom decks (Deckbuilding); very few amount of cards that you are capable of unlocking (298). This game could benefit from alot more for more deckbuilding options.
- The AI however does have these decks with extra cards so you will get very frustrated playing those decks YOU want to build yourself but can't when you are playing through the main campaign.
-There just isnt enough of the cards of a particular type to build a deck thats fun. You can't even get a Doomblade or Pacifism. Lol.
- Pay to win "premium boosters". Truly not needed.
So even with the many CONS outweighing the PROS I still find this game fun. I just really hope WotC come out with a much needed update.

There seems to be a lot of hate reviews on this game. Tons of people buy the game and then return it after playing required minutes to write a review. As a result they are spreading misinformation because they didn't even bother to fully play the game.
Microtransactions:
First of all gear and feats aren't active in 1v1 and 2v2 modes. Only place you can use them are 4v4 matches. The game's combat wasn't even designed for 4v4 modes. 4v4 is just one giant gank fest.
Second, gear scales with your level. Even if you buy tons of packs at low level, higher level players will have better gear than you. You can't even get rare gear before prestige 1.
Plus the gear isn't like the gear in rpgs or mmos. It gives you stats on one area and then reduces the stats on something else. For example, a gear might help you get into revenge mode faster but in return your attacks will be less powerfull. Feats unlock really fast. I don't see the point of buying them.
DLC:
All the new content is free. Season pass only lets you get the heroes one week early without paying in-game currency. In order to play with a hero, you DO NOT need to buy them even with in-game currency. You need to buy heroes only if you want to customize them or gear them up. If you are a player like me that only cares about 1v1 and 2v2s you don't even need to buy the heroes.
Combat:
The fighting mechanics are really good and in-depth. If you are a player that dies to spam, guard breaks etc. it just means you don't know how to fight back. If the opponent is spamming attacks, block/parry to get your opening and punish.
Don't stand right next to a cliff, sharp objects etc. and when they guard break, either guard break them back or just hit them with a light attack before it lands.
Most of the time, i give my opponent enough space so they can get out of the *danger area*, i don't guard break towards the cliff but they insist on staying so close to edge they fall off after powerfull attacks. Then they cry and rant about it.
P2P:
Even tho i had connection issues on 4v4 modes in the open beta, i didn't have any issues in the actual game. So i don't have any issues but i can't speak for everyone.

Alright, time to get a review on. I am here today to give a review to a game I don't think gets enough credit for what it does. Are you ready? Good! The game that we are going to dive into today is none other then Dawn of Fantasy Kingdom Wars. If you are not excited and you love strategy games you need to get excited because this game brings so much to the table. First off we have three different races to choose from humans, orcs, and elves, the later of which I am currently enjoying. These races are different in just enough ways to make you want to keep coming back for more. The humans may be versatile, where the orcs are tough and brutal and the elves are elegant. Don't fret there is no need to be careful on what race you pick you can have multiple armies and city's that you have built. I believe that having multiple armies is good for the game it keeps it fresh, I also like the looks on each races cities. Be careful here you can easily sink hours into the game just creating your city. This game is solid in all aspects of strategy, story, and mind numbing sieging for those of you who just want to get straight to the action. You also get heroic units that allow for fun, Mages, Minotaur, Dragons, and many other goodies. You can also customize your cities the more you put in the better your people will be protected! Now the game does have some bugs that can be frustrating. The game doesn't give you an option on whether or not you wish to participate in pvp all though it offers a buy out for the siege it does get frustrating when you are in the middle of building and you get attacked. I have listed the Pros and the Cons of this game but in all honestly you need to pick the game up its free on steam and decide for you self whether this is a go or a dump. This game does allow you to bring friends along on a siege so dust off your armor and lets get ready to go to war!  If I was to rate this game I would give it a solid 7.5 out of 10 the game has to much replay value and is definitely a trend setter in the strategy game department.

Shadow Warrior 2 is a fast paced first person shooter with loot found in random chests, bought in stores, given as quest rewards, or even found after killing a boss. The dynamic gore system is awesome in the way that you can damage and kill your enemies while leaving limbs and big chunks of flesh everywhere. Some enemies can be rather annoying with their high elemental resistance, though stronger gems and certain perks can help with this. The co-op in SW2 is fun, when it works. One player hosts, while the other player(s) join the game. Enemies gain increased health and players gain karma (experience points faster). The variety of guns and blades is really good, though it would be nice if the sniper rifle equivalent weapons spent less ammo per shot, carried more ammo, and could damage enemies from further away.
While the partially randomized nature of the levels and all too common level pieces can become boring after awhile, I still have found new parts of old levels on a new playthrough.
I would give this game a solid 8/10.

An impressive total conversion mod for Amnesia: The Dark Descent -- though probably only worthwhile if you've played the original Penumbra series -- this is a particularly good way to wash away the aftertaste from the marginally enjoyable third game in the series, Penumbra: Requiem.  The modmakers have an obvious love for the source material; and even though they take a few small liberties with the story, I found myself pulled back into a universe of memories (and fears) I hadn't realized I still retain.
The two most noticeable shortcomings in this outing are 1) awkward and sometimes cringe-worthy English translation (and voice-acting) of dialogue and text; and 2) a few too many of the enemy encounters feel unnecessarily unbalanced, where either the monsters are scripted to be unavoidable or seem to be slightly psychic about the player's location (I'm uncertain if the latter is an authentic remnant of the original Penumbra games or an addition for the mod).  Even so, Necrologue is a remarkably polished and consistent experience... and a worthy tribute to the early works of Frictional Games.

Preordered this game and still don't regret it for a second.
The gunplay is visceral and satisfying, and the swordplay and melee is frantic and fun. Movement is fast paced with double jumps and dashes, and there is no cover or chest high walls anywhere in sight. It reminds me of Unreal Tournament with its double dodge, and more recently DOOM with the fast paced movement and hordes of enemies.
You can upgrade your supernatural skills and your weapons, adding in more damage or doing elemental damage, or even dual wielding guns or throwing them out as turrets. You have your normal elemental types, like fire and ice (which'll slow enemies), and you can make enemies' bodies explode when killed by caustic. And there are a whole range of guns you can find and use, different level mods you can find (and later on grind together for better quality output), or just sell outright to a vendor. Pistols, SMGs, Rifles, heavy machine guns, shotguns, swords, chainsaws, chainsaw-swords, bows, laser weapons, grenade launchers, rocket launchers and more. You can turn invisible, go into a rage and do more damage while taking less, you can impale enemies on spikes, freezing them in place, or push them all back so they fall over and become stunned for a while. You can even drain health from enemies.
Maps have random sections that are generated, so each playthrough will have different areas, or locations of loot and chests, as well as enemies. Most maps also have a special or mini-boss each, which can drop a special weapon (as well as an achievement). Sometimes the foliage can become a little hard to see through, but you do have a minimap that'll show red dots to where enemies are (should show up even if you can't see them). The map also shows loot that you may have overlooked, or a chest you still have to open. And you can replay maps again and again once you finish with 'em.
There's a story here, too, but if you just want to get to the "good" parts you can skip most dialogue if you want.

First up: What is it with these European game designers who insist upon doing English voice-acting parts themselves?  And do they never watch American films, so they might have a better idea how to pronounce certain words?!  Surely somewhere over the width and breadth of the internet - I'M always available! - they could find someone for whom English is a first language who'll do some voice parts for them.  The dude doing an impersonation of everyone's favourite monkey-hating virus, Clarence, at least does a serviceable job, but he's still not as good as the original guy.  Anyway, that's some of the bad stuff out of the way, now onto the good stuff...
The Penumbra series was, as we all know, Frictional's precursor - downright TEST RUN, if you want my two cents - to their far more famous Amnesia: The Dark Descent.  Simply put, without the trio of Penumbras to cut their development teeth on, Amnesia would not have come into the world in such an almost flawlessly-formed shape.  The "fans" who have made Necrologue are certainly aware of this history, and have in many ways set out to make a Penumbra game with the HINDSIGHT that the more polished Amnesia can now give them.
Take lighting for instance: In the Penumbra games, you never really worried about conserving lighting because, frankly, the glowstick was just as useful as the flashlight and didn't need to be constantly refilled with batteries.  It wasn't until The Dark Descent that the good people at Frictional fully realised just how scary threatened lack of lighting in a horror game could BE...and the makers of Necrologue throw down the gauntlet in this regard nice an' quickly by giving us only a half-empty flashlight with which to begin our explorations (lying near to which is a dead-as-a-dodo glowstick with not an an ounce of greeny goodness in it, just to rub it in)!  They then proceed to make sure that if we don't conserve the batteries we intermittently find thereafter, we'll be down to troublesome, unwanted-attention-grabbing flares in no time, and after that...well, perpetual near-darkness, one supposes!  (Fortunately, I have yet to reach THAT hopeless stage.)
This game also uses Amnesia's superior graphics, lusher scenery and "eyes-more-slowly-adjusting-to-the-gloom" mechanics (or did I just imagine that one?) to excellent effect, without wasting its time adopting the borderline-pointless "sanity" system which Amnesia used to such minimal effect (I only recall succumbing "badly" to the effects of said sanity loss ONCE in my two playthroughs of said game).  And yes, the healing items are again in excessive supply, considering that one hardly even gets the CHANCE to heal in games brimming with enemies who can kill you with one or two blows (but we probably shouldn't look a gift horse in the mouth).
All that aside, this is DEFINITELY a Penumbra game, seeing the return of a lot of our old favourites:  Monster dogs, giant spiders, dissected worms, alien foetuses in jars, bizarre cylindrical artifacts doubling as save points, science-y puzzles which you'll probably find hard if (like me) you're actually useless at science, generators and valves and switches galore, and let's not forget being chased by creepy naked dudes with overgrown umbilical cords...you name it, it's pretty much all here.  There's also some of that old-fashioned frustration on offer - there's a bit involving three fuses and a generator which, as far as I can tell, I completely ♥♥♥♥ed by flicking a switch at the wrong time, blowing one of the fuses and forcing me to go back a few saves - but on the whole, it's pretty safe to say that if you enjoyed the "official" Penumbra games, you'll almost certainly enjoy this one also.  I mean, what's an adventure game without a few hair-tearingly annoying bits where you either feel like giving up altogether, or at the very least succumbing to the evil urge to look at someone else's walkthrough.  Answer: Well, an EASY adventure game, I suppose.  Oh, and the "I hate linear games" people are gonna LOVE this one, by the way.  Every time you walk through a DOOR you have four new corridors and fourteen new doors to try out (okay, so I'm exaggerating, but only very slightly)...
Overall, a very worthy "fan-made" chapter in the Penumbra saga; one not necessarily any better or worse than the three official games which preceded it, though it does perhaps make for a slightly more "satisfying" conclusion than Frictional's own (anti-)climactic chapter, Requiem (which chose to eliminate all life-threatening "horror" elements in favour of fiendish puzzles and the occasional environmental hazard).  Here's hoping that some of the talent behind this mod will make an original horror game or two of their own day some day, as they certainly seem to know what they're doing on the strength of this one.
Verdict: 8.5/10.

This time in a Choose Your Own Adventure game by
, you play as the world's second-best jewel thief planning a heist of the most dangerous diamond ever known. Travel the world while you slowly gather your team together, one by one -- old friends, old lovers, and perhaps even old enemies. Do some spywork, inflitrate the mansion in which the diamond is kept, flirt with your team members, evade your police inspector nemesis...
This story contains every heist/spy trope in the book, including car chase scenes, sexy clothing, and lots and lots of charisma. And it's downright
.
+ Action! Guns! Chase scenes! Riches beyond your imagination!
+ Scheming rival who steals all your targets away from under your nose
+ Option to stab your team in the back if you want to
- At 100,000 words, it's significantly shorter than other games in the CoG lineup
- Due to its large use of heist/thief genre tropes, the story is very predictable
- Not a lot of depth or deep connection between the characters
- Not a lot of alternative routes or endings; your choices don't have that much effect
- Limited romance options
- No save points
Personally, I enjoyed it a lot because it was what I was looking for -- simple, clean fun, and a charming albeit short heist story. However, I would've still liked to see multiple alternative endings; the fact that your choices don't seem to affect the story much this time around is probably the biggest downside of this game for me. If the theme doesn't fit you, you're probably better off picking another interactive novel game. If not: have fun stealing stuff!
